subject: Discovery recap: Inference cost pressure / unit economics (FinBot)
messages:
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finbot.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Park <elena@finbot.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Mar 2026 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro / demo — notes

Thanks for the demo earlier — good run-through. A quick summary from our side and a few clarifying Qs so we can align on economics and next steps.

High-level pain / goals:
- Unit cost of inference is a top constraint — our current per-request cost for short chat responses (~40 tokens) is eating into margin as we scale.
- We need predictable cost per 1k responses and options to tune latency vs cost for lower-value flows.
- Compliance: data residency and audit logs matter but we can discuss later in procurement.

Current stack:
- Models: mixture of hosted open models (LLM-X, Llama-variant) via provider A; some on-prem experiments.
- Serving: sitting behind a homegrown router; no production KV cache, batching is manual via a queue.
- Quantization: we've done 8-bit for experiments but not confident in quality or integration effort.

Questions / clarifications for Redwood team:
1) Can you share an example unit-cost calc for 40-token responses vs 200-token responses (including batching/caching assumptions)?
2) How much work to enable prefix/KV caching for our conversational flows?
3) What's the support/rollout path if we want to test quantized model variants in a canary?

Next steps from FinBot: want a short MPP (mutual plan) with technical success criteria and an estimate for savings if we adopt Redwood's caching + batching recommendations.

— Alex
Alex Johnson | Head of Platform, FinBot.ai
alex.johnson@finbot.ai | +1 415-555-0132

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finbot.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Elena Park <elena@finbot.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Mar 2026 17:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Inference cost pressure / unit economics (FinBot)

Alex — thanks for the thoughtful recap and the questions. Appreciate you outlining the success criteria. Below is a concise recap from our discovery call + answers to your Qs and proposed next steps so we have alignment.

Recap of pain & goals (what we heard)
- Main goal: reduce per-interaction inference cost while keeping sub-100ms median latency for web chat and acceptable latency for async batch flows.
- Constraints: limited existing batching/caching, some willingness to try quantized variants if quality holds.
- Success criteria (suggested): 30–50% unit cost reduction for low-complexity chat flows at <=100ms p50; end-to-end SLOs and quantization regression <2% on your eval prompts.

Quick answers to your Qs:
1) Unit-cost example: attached is an initial back-of-envelope pricing sheet and a sample MAU estimate (redwood_pricing_sheet_v1.pdf, mau_estimate_q1.csv). Assumptions included:
   - Baseline: single-request, no batching, 40 tokens per response, baseline model A (float16) on gpus X.
   - Redwood optimized path: 1) prefix/KV caching on conversational families; 2) continuous batching for background low-priority traffic; 3) option to route low-value flows to smaller quantized variants.
   - Example delta: for 40-token web chat, estimated unit cost reduction 35% with caching + batching; for 200-token generation, reduction ~20% (depends on workload mix).
2) Caching: enabling prefix/KV caching typically takes 2–4 engineering days to integrate our client-side hints + server-side keys for session affinity; end-to-end validation (QA + perf) ~2 weeks.
3) Quantization canaries: we have an established canary path — create a quantized model variant, run A/B on a subset of traffic, and compare on your eval set. We can automate rollbacks if quality dips. Time to first canary: ~1–3 weeks depending on model onboarding.

Proposed next steps (mutual action plan):
- Redwood: provide detailed unit-cost workbook and an initial config suggestion (batching thresholds, cache TTLs, candidate quantization profiles) — deliver by 2026-03-30.
- FinBot: share a sample eval prompt set and representative traffic distribution (tokens per request, % chat vs generation) — target by 2026-03-29.
- Joint: 30-minute follow-up next week to align on success metrics and scheduling a 2-week canary test window.

If this reads correctly I can follow up with a short MPP doc and shared HubSpot record.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (650) 555-0199

Attachment: mau_estimate_q1.csv (sample MAU/traffic estimate)

From: Elena Park <elena@finbot.ai>

Date: Thu, 26 Mar 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Inference cost pressure / unit economics (FinBot)

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful. A couple of clarifications from our engineering side after reviewing the pricing sheet:
- We currently batch at the app layer for async jobs but not for our low-latency web chat. Curious how Redwood's continuous batching will avoid adding p50 latency to web traffic (is it priority-aware?).
- For KV caching: do you require session affinity or do you support keyed, multi-tenant caches? We need to avoid per-tenant cache blowup.

Also — happy to share the eval prompt set (we have ~200 seed prompts that represent the worst-case quality scenarios). Will upload to the shared Drive and post the link.

Elena
Senior SRE, FinBot.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena@finbot.ai>, Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finbot.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Inference cost pressure / unit economics (FinBot)

Elena — great questions, short answers here and we can include technical docs in the MPP pack.
- Continuous batching is workload-aware and priority-aware: latency-sensitive web chat is served on hot-path lanes with lower batch-hold windows; background/async traffic is batched more aggressively. We can tune thresholds during the canary.
- KV caching supports keyed multi-tenant caches and TTLs per namespace; we also provide eviction metrics so you can monitor per-tenant cache pressure. Default pattern doesn't require strict session affinity — we support both affinity and hashed-key approaches.

Next immediate actions:
- Marissa to share the MPP + detailed cost workbook by 2026-03-30 (I will attach docs to the HubSpot record).
- FinBot to upload their eval prompts and traffic sample (Elena / Alex) by 2026-03-29.
- Schedule 30-min sync: proposed Mon 2026-03-29 10:00am PT — I will send a calendar invite pending your confirmation.

Ben/Vivek — looping you both for visibility on the canary path and any initial resource sizing suggestions.

Thanks — speak soon,
Marissa
